entities.name: Marcus Ummidius Quadratus Annianus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Ummidius Quadratus Annianus (138–182) was a Roman Senator and the nephew of the Emperor Marcus Aurelius. Born into a prominent family, he was educated in the classical tradition and served in various administrative roles throughout the Roman Empire. His involvement in an unsuccessful plot to assassinate his cousin, the Emperor Commodus, led to his execution in 182 CE. Annianus's actions, though ultimately unsuccessful, reflect the complexities and tensions within the Roman imperial family during this period.

Annianus's significance lies in his role as a representative of the senatorial class and his connection to the imperial family. His actions, though small compared to the grandeur of the Roman Empire, demonstrate the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that characterized Roman politics during this era.

The legacy of Marcus Ummidius Quadratus Annianus can be seen in the continued influence of the Roman Senate on Western politics and the enduring fascination with the imperial family's personal struggles and power struggles.
